chunks: He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad reported to me, he said: Abu Abdillah Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani narrated to us, he said: Isa ibn Mehran narrated to us, he said: Hafs ibn Umar al-Farra informed us, he said: Abu Mu'adh al-Khazzaz informed us from Ubaydullah ibn Ahmad al-Rab'i, who said:

While Ibn Abbas was addressing the people of Basrah, he turned toward them face to face and said: "O community confused about its faith! Had you given precedence to whom Allah gave precedence, and kept back whom Allah kept back, and placed the inheritance and the authority where Allah placed them, then no share from the obligatory portions ordained by Allah would have devolved upon distant relatives, nor would the friend of Allah have been deprived, nor would two persons have ever differed about a divine ruling, nor would the community have disputed about anything from the Book of Allah.
So taste the evil consequence of what you have neglected through what your own hands have wrought.
And those who have done injustice shall soon know what fate awaits them.

key_terms.الوراثة: Inheritance, here referring to the prophetic inheritance of leadership
key_terms.ولي الله: The friend/guardian of Allah, referring to the rightful successor

ai.seo_question: What did Ibn Abbas say about the succession and Khilafah in Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Amali of al-Mufid, Ibn Abbas (the Prophet's cousin and eminent Quran exegete) delivers a powerful public address in Basrah during his governorship under Imam Ali. He rebukes the Muslim community for deviating from the divinely ordained succession, arguing that had they upheld the rightful leadership and inheritance designated by Allah, there would have been no discord in religious rulings or disputes over the Quran. He warns them of the consequences of their neglect, concluding with Quran 26:227 threatening those who committed injustice.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 7. He said: Abu Hafs Umar ibn Muhammad reported to me from Abu Abdillah Ja’far ibn Muhammad al-Hasani, who reported from Isa ibn Mehran, who reported from Hafs ibn Umar al-Farra, who reported from Abu Muaz al-Khazzaz from Ubaidullah ibn Ahmad al-Rab’ai, who said:

While Ibn Abbas addressed the people of Basrah, when he came face to face with them, he said: "O people who are lost and confused about its faith, if you had given precedence to him who Allah had preferred, and if you had kept back him who Allah had kept back, and if you had kept the inheritance and the authority where Allah had kept them, then the share (in inheritance) ordained by Allah would not have devolved upon distant relatives (leaving behind the actual heirs), nor would the Wali of Allah have been deprived; and no two persons would have ever differed about a divine order, nor would the Ummah enter into any disputations about any interpretation of the Book of Allah.
So now, have a taste of the evil consequence earned by your disregard, and by your own hands.
And those who do injustice shall soon come to know what punishment awaits them."
